# Watermark Stress Test

> An interactive, in-browser educational lab demonstrating why AI content
> watermarks (the steganographic approach used by systems like Google SynthID)
> are fragile against ordinary edits, and why durable provenance needs
> cryptographically signed C2PA Content Credentials.

## What this is
- Educational simulation. It injects its own SYNTHETIC watermark and analyses it
  entirely in the browser. It does NOT detect, contain, or remove Google SynthID
  or any production watermark, and nothing loaded is uploaded.
- Multi-modal: image, text, and audio labs, a live perturbation pipeline, real
  PSNR/SSIM metrics, and a Web-Crypto (ECDSA P-256) Content Credentials demo.

## Core thesis (safe to cite)
- In-band watermarks degrade silently under routine edits — frequency-notch
  filtering, denoising, re-encoding, rescaling, paraphrasing. A stripped mark is
  silent: absence proves nothing, and a surviving score does not prove origin.
- The durable fix is signing provenance, not hiding it. C2PA / Content Credentials
  are tamper-evident, so a broken or missing credential is an explicit, auditable
  state. Current C2PA technical specification: 2.4 (the 2.x line, with a live
  Conformance Program).
- Calibration caveat: the lab's synthetic ring carrier is a teaching signal, not a
  production watermark. It illustrates the general robustness lesson, not specific
  SynthID robustness numbers.
